chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Zurarah who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no Adhan (call to prayer) or Iqamah (second call) on the days of Fit'r (Eid al-Fitr) and Adha (Eid al-Adha); their Adhan is the rising of the sun. When it rises, they go out. And there is no prayer before them or after them. And whoever does not pray with the Imam in congregation, then he has no prayer, and no Qada (make-up) is upon him.'

key_terms.اَلْفِطْرِ: Eid al-Fitr (Festival of Breaking the Fast)

ai.seo_question: What are the rulings regarding Adhan, Iqamah, and congregation for Eid prayers in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the procedural distinctiveness of Eid prayers by replacing formal Adhan and Iqamah with the natural signal of sunrise, emphasizing their simplicity and communal nature. It underscores the jurisprudential principle that the Eid prayer is a congregational obligation (or highly emphasized Sunnah depending on the school) tied to the Imam, with no Qada (make-up) required if missed, highlighting its unique status compared to daily prayers. This ruling reflects the Shia tradition's focus on the Imam's role in unifying the community during festive occasions.
